Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on April 1, 2021 via
Zoom. Sabrina Barnes called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Director
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  None

Public Comments

  None

Selection of the Chair

  Sabrina Barnes stated per the Inglewood Municipal Code (Section 2-92. Organization.), “The
Park and Recreation Commission shall select from its members a chairperson and a vice
chairperson, who shall serve, respectively, as such, during the pleasure of the Commission.” Two of
you have expressed an interest in serving as Chair of the Park and Recreation Commission. Each
candidate will be given three (3) minutes max to make a statement about their respective interest.
Following the comment period, the Commissioners will vote. This is not a vote by the public. Only
the Park and Recreation Commissioners may vote. We will use the Zoom poll option. The
Commissioner with the most votes will serve as Chair; the Commissioner with the second highest
votes will serve as Vice-Chair.

  The candidates (in alphabetical order) are Commissioner Henry Brown and Commissioner
Lee Denmon. Commissioner Brown gave a brief statement followed by Commissioner Denmon.
Sabrina Barnes thanked the Commissioners and opened the poll for the Commission to cast their
vote. Everyone could see the poll but only the Commissioners could vote. Following the vote where
Commissioner Denman received the majority vote (2 – Brown; 3- Denmon) Sabrina Barnes
congratulated and introduced Chairman Denmon and Vice Chairman Brown.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

  Sabrina Barnes welcomed the newly appointed District Four and At-Large Commissioners.
District Four Commissioner Beck introduced himself and stated he is excited to be apart of the
Commission and is looking forward to serving and working with everyone.

  Commissioner Brown (At-Large) stated he fully supports the Chair and is looking forward to
the upcoming 2022 Super Bowl and 2024 Olympics along with everything exciting to come.

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the minutes from March 5, 2020.
Commissioner Denmon seconded, and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck, Brown and Denmon
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment Four of the Elderly
Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number ENP202107 with County of Los Angeles Workforce
Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to reflect award of additional funding for
provision of the Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of $105,101 (Grants Fund).

  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner McLemore
seconded, and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck, Brown and Denmon
  Nays: None

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission receive and file the staff report regarding the ordinance amending Inglewood Municipal
Code (I.M.C.) Section 5-67 (Unauthorized Use of Park Facilities Prohibited) which defines the terms
“camp or lodge,” expand hours when people are prohibited from being in City Parks and updates a
job title. Commissioner Denmon stated the Commission will receive and file the report.

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions: a) Award a
contract and approve a three (3) year agreement with Premier Property Preservation, LLC to provide
janitorial services for City exterior park facilities in the annual amount of $550,872; total amount of
three-year agreement is $1,652,616; and b) Authorize use of the COVID account in the amount of
$321,342 for payments for April 2021-September 2021, and $149,909.18 for payment for janitorial

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

cleaning for exterior restrooms for the months of November 2020, December 2020, January 2021
and February 2021.

  Commissioner Beck asked if it is $550,872 times three (3) that gives you $1,652,616 were
previously allocated to clean the restrooms and the additional $550,000 is for moving forward. Ms.
Barnes stated correct. Commissioner Beck asked if the $550,000 is the flat rate, would there be any
increase if this is voted as a three (3) year commitment, and are there no additional costs associated
with a yes vote. Ms. Barnes stated as long as the scope of work remains the same referring to the
CDC (Centers for Disease Control & Prevention) and Public Health guidelines. The initial cleaning
requirement was three (3) times a day and now it has been changed to five (5) times a day.
Commissioner Beck asked if the guidelines were to change would there be an option for the
Commission to meet again and discuss. Ms. Barnes stated there would be a negotiation with the
vendor regarding the additional scope of work, associated cost, and an amendment to the
agreement. Ms. Barnes made a correction noting the Public County Health suggests hourly cleaning
of the restrooms.

  Commissioner Beck made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner McLemore
seconded and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck, Brown and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   All playgrounds and fitness stations are now open to the public as of March 16, 2021. The
  rims for all basketball courts will be reinstalled beginning next week. With that, all outdoor
  amenities will be available for use by the public. Most of them have been closed since March
  2020.
   New part-time staff has been hired to help with maintenance of the center medians.
   The Parks Section will oversee the new janitorial contract. In addition to cleaning the
  restrooms, the company will also be responsible for the closing of restrooms. Park
  Maintenance staff is responsible for opening restrooms.
   Graffiti has been on the rise in all districts and at all parks since the beginning of the year.
  Vincent Park is one of the main parks that has been targeted daily. It seems like the rise in
  graffiti is due to neighboring gangs crossing over into our city and tagging. If you have a
  graffiti compliant, you can call us at graffiti hotline at 310-412-8739. Leave a message with
  address and description of the location.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the following:
 Park Reopening Update: While the indoor parks and recreation centers remain closed, we
  are happy to report that many of our outdoor amenities have reopened. This includes
  playgrounds, skate parks, basketball courts, tennis courts, exercise equipment, pickle ball,
  baseball diamonds and multi-purpose fields. Patrons are required to wear face coverings
  and practice social distancing.
 Instructor Recruitment: The department is currently seeking instructors to provide classes
  and workshops that enhance the quality of life for toddlers, youth, adults, and senior citizens.
  We are looking for instructors to teach various classes such as dance, health and wellness,
  music, performing arts, physical fitness, technology, and special interest. Interested
  individuals can obtain instructor guidelines and application on the city’s website on the parks
  and recreation homepage. Although our indoor facilities remain closed, the goal is to have
  classes in place and ready to go when we are given the green light to reopen indoors.
 Athletic Field Rentals: Our baseball, softball and multi-purpose fields are open and available
  for rental. Use of the fields is by reservation and permit only. Reservation packets are
  available online, on the parks and recreation homepage. All applications must be submitted
  online.
 Co-ed Sports Clinics: The sports division is currently offering FREE cod-ed sports
  conditioning clinics for boys and girls ages 8-14 at Edward Vincent Park on Saturday, April
  3 and 10. Clinics one hour and offered in two sessions: 11:15 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. or 12:30
  p.m. to 1:30 p.m. All clinics are FREE! Pre-registration is required online at
  cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com.
 Every Body Plays Program: The department is excited to announce that we have partnered
  with LA County Parks and Recreation and 25 other cities, joining a movement to get kids
  playing at our parks again. The program, titled Every Body Plays, encourages youth and
  families to get active, play and visit our parks. While visiting our parks, they will have the
  ability to check out selected equipment at no charge. The process is easy and only requires
  patrons to simply present a school or other form of I.D. to check equipment out. There will
  be a variety of equipment to choose from including balls, racquets, frisbee, jump ropes, hula
  hoops, carom boards and games, to name a few. The program will begin on Monday, April
  12 at both Rogers and Darby Parks. The program will operate Monday through Friday from
  3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. The program will also be offered at Ashwood, Center and North Parks
  beginning Monday, April 19 and will culminate at all parks on June 12. We will be at Ashwood
  Park: Wednesday from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. and Saturdays from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.,
  at Center Park: Monday and Thursday from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. and at North Park:
  Tuesday and Friday 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
 Self-Defense Classes: the department is proud to offer FREE outdoor self-defense classes
  at Center Park every 2nd and 4th Saturday of the month. Classes are one (1) hour, from
  11:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon. Families are encouraged to attend. The minimum age

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

  requirement is 4 years. Classes will begin on Saturday, April 10 and will culminate June 26,
  2021. Pre-registration is required. Register on-line at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Our Nutrition program increased enrollment from 300 clients to over 800 clients during
  COVID-19 to accommodate the sudden increase in program demand. Throughout the
  pandemic, no waitlist has been required and every eligible senior who applied for meals
  received them. This week marks the 1st anniversary of the ENP program changing to
  accommodate the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, and we have delivered a total of
  300,000 meal packages (packs of 5, 7, or 21) throughout the year. Currently, 500 seniors
  are enrolled in the program. At the peak of the pandemic, we increased our program to
  include breakfast, lunch, and dinner, as well as monthly shelf-stable packages and weekly
  fresh produce delivery. The City of Inglewood’s ENP is the only ENP in the entire County of
  Los Angeles which has served three meals per day and adhered to the county certified
  menu, while also not resorting to a waitlist. Our nutrition staff continues to deliver weekly
  fresh produce to our seniors by partnering with Social Justice Learning Institute. Our staff
  continues to work every day to deliver meals to meet our senior’s needs. Our Nutrition
  Program continues to find outside resources and donations from organizations such as LA
  County, Sofi Stadium, and Social Justice Learning Institute. The nutrition program recently
  delivered a festive bag with nuts, fruits, mints, masks, face shields, and sanitizer to our
  seniors.
   On Tuesday, March 9 and 11, the Inglewood Senior Center hosted Ambulance CARE who
  provided the Moderna vaccine to 172 seniors. The event went very well, and the second
  shot will be provided on April 6, 2021 to the seniors who participated with the initial shot.
   The Inglewood Senior Center is offering Virtual Classes for seniors. Senior Center staff in
  collaboration with the city’s Video Production team has been able to provide and offer virtual
  workout classes that consist of: Zumba, Tai-Chi, Salsa, Chair Exercises and Line Dancing.
   Our Transportation Program continues to provide senior trips to dialysis and critical doctors’
  appointments. All our drivers are currently scheduled daily to deliver meals or transport
  seniors to medical appointments.
   The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) will operate Monday through Friday, from
  May 3, 2021 through June 11, 2021 at Rogers and Darby Parks. Kids will be receiving supper
  and snacks from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. on a first come first serve basis. Staff mandatory
  training is scheduled for April 20, 2021. Training will consist of operational safety procedures
  including new COVID-19 procedures.
   Summer Food Summer Program (SFSP) will operate at the city’s parks and Community
  Centers five (5) days a week, Monday through Friday, from June 14, 2021 through August
  31, 2021. We will be providing breakfast from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., lunch and snacks
  from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the following sites: Ashwood Park, Crenshaw-Imperial
  Library, Darby Park, Edward Vincent, Jr. Park, Inglewood Main Library, Lockhaven
  Community Center, North Park, Rogers Park and Siminski Park.

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

    Although the Senior Center is closed to the public, staff is still working daily. If you have any
  questions, we can be reached at (310) 412-5338.

Directors Report

Sabrina Barnes gave an update on the following Capital Improvement Projects:
   Vincent Park Swimming Pool Resurfacing Project started in March of 2020 and was
  completed in June of 2020. The scope of work included the complete resurfacing of both
  the lap pool and wading pool. Also, in relation to the pool complex, all wrought iron
  fencing has been replaced in the interest of strengthening the safety of the perimeter of
  the pool.
   Rogers Park Restroom Renovation Project began in the Fall of 2020. The project
  provided for the demolition of the existing restroom and construction of a new restroom
  with the completion date set for the end of this month. The new restrooms are the City’s
  new standard vault type system model, meaning they are private individual units with a
  private bathroom seat, a handwashing station with all the amenities in one private room.
  The city is expecting to begin a second restroom renovation project at Edward Vincent
  Park this summer, renovating the restrooms located near the amphitheater and picnic
  areas (our highest used area). Staff is currently working on bid specifications with the
  goal of releasing the bid document no later than May 2021 with the expectation to be
  contracted and ready to go before the end of this fiscal year, September 30th.
   The tennis complex at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park was opened, renamed, and rededicated
  in honor of Donald Bly, a longtime volunteer and past city employee two (2) years ago.
  Since that time, the city has contracted with the 40 Love Foundation who is responsible
  for managing the city’s tennis program. Phase Two (2) of renovations has recently taken
  place. It is a smaller project consisting of a new set of benches added to each one of
  the courts and addressing plumbing matters to assist in better maintaining the facility.
  Work is scheduled to be completed within the next two (2) weeks.
   On January 12, 2021, the Inglewood City Council approved an agreement between the
  City of Inglewood and the Grow Cycling Foundation for the installation of a pump track
  at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park. The action will provide for a new and exciting amenity at
  the park. Grow Cycling is a registered 501(c)(3) organization created to establish a new
  avenue for inclusion and build career development in the cycling industry as well as
  empower existing programs working to tear down barriers to entry and cycling for
  marginalized communities. In short, the foundation works to improve the diversity in the
  cycling in the industry, promoting education, access, and opportunities for inclusion. The
  pump track will be 100% financed. The track was awarded to the park by Growth Cycling
  and will be constructed by Bellow Solutions, the sole contractor for Red Bull competition
  pump tracks. Once the track is completed it will put the city in line to host Red Bull
  Competitions at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park. Growth Cycling was founded by Elliot
  Jackson, a former World Cup downhill mountain bike racer, a commentator for Red Bull
  television and an entrepreneur. The track will be approximately 10,000 to 12,000 square

  6
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

  feet and the estimated at 1.2 million dollars. The project is currently in the design phase
  with a goal to begin construction by September.
    The city has been awarded Measure A funding, per Capita funding that is received
  based on the city’s population. In the coming months, staff will coordinate community
  outreach meetings regarding the measure’s funding. In order to utilize the funds, there
  has to be an application with an outline of the projects we want to undertake and also
  show that the community was involved in the planning of the effort. We will be holding
  focus groups, including conversations in upcoming Park and Recreation Commission
  meetings as well as attending Town Hall meetings hosted by our City Council Members.
  The goal is to get the community to weigh in on the actual project so there is some
  ownership. About five (5) years ago, the department conducted a community wide parks
  need assessment where 10 priorities were put in place including renovating the multi-
  purpose fields, upgrading the restrooms at the parks, the tennis courts.
    Another improvement project we have done consisted of installation of cameras at
  various parks. The next park on schedule to have cameras installed is Darby Park,
  installation is scheduled to begin the week of April 6. The camera system includes a 10-
  camera outdoor system that will cover the general grounds, parking lots and building
  entry points. Following that installation, we will be going before the Council to have a
  contract awarded to secure cameras for Edward Vincent, Jr. Park.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner Brown thanked and appreciated staff for their work on the senior meal
program. He has 500 facemasks he would like to donate to the city and has opportunity for individuals
in need of COVID-19 testing upon returning to work. Ms. Barnes stated her staff is awesome, real
troopers who go above and beyond to make sure the city is well served. She called out the Human
Services Division, Thomas Uwal and his staff stating while other city staff has had the opportunity to
work remotely and despite the pandemic, he and his staff have not missed a beat by personally
delivering 300,000 meals during this time. Commissioner Denmon thanked Mr. Uwal and his staff.
Mr. Uwal thanked Ms. Barnes for her leadership and for being by their side every step of the way.

  Commissioner McLemore thanked Sabrina Barnes, Stephanie Maldonado and all the staff
for their reports. She also welcomed Commissioners Beck and Brown and congratulated the new
Chair, Commissioner Denmon.

  Commissioner Brown is looking forward to moving forward with the tremendous
Parks and Recreation Department.

  7
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES April 1, 2021

  Commissioner Beck thanked the Commissioners for welcoming him and the staff for their
reports given this evening. He really looks forward to working with everyone.

  Commissioner Denmon thanked everyone for attending and is glad to have all positions filled so
they can get to work. He commended the department’s staff for all their hardwork.

  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 7:02 p.m.
